subject: [hw] IV -> V02: after a recovered nested stop, the outer UNDEF reports the last pc with the first insn
body:
Minor reporting defect, no emulation change: c->stop_insn and c->stop_addr can come from two different failures.

Scenario (real vpud, host, current tree):
 - guest main runs inside sh_libc_init()s n2a32_call; at libvcodec_utility.so:drv_getchipname+0x31 (guest 0x40354fc2) the T16 word 0xb318 is UNDEF: the inner run sets stop=UNDEF, stop_insn=0xb318, stop_addr=0x40354fc2.
 - sh_libc_init sees the stop, returns 0 to the guest _start; the outer run continues (no stop_request).
 - at vpud+0x284e (0xbbe8, also UNDEF) the class fails; n2a32_run does
       if (c->stop == N2A32_STOP_NONE) c->stop = N2A32_STOP_UNDEF;
       if (c->stop_insn == 0) c->stop_insn = insn;
       c->stop_addr = pc;
   so stop stays UNDEF, stop_insn stays 0xb318 (first) and stop_addr becomes 0x4008284e (last).

The runner reports "UNDEF 0x0000b318 at 0x4008284e", which reads like a 0xb318 word at 0x284e; the memory there is 0xbbe8. It cost me ten minutes and will cost every worker who reads a stop line.

Two possible contracts, either is fine:
 (a) first failure wins entirely: only overwrite stop_insn/stop_addr when c->stop == NONE at the top of that block (and do not overwrite addr afterwards);
 (b) last failure wins entirely: always set both.
I would pick (a) and say so in n2a32.h, since the first stop is the one the shim could not recover from in the general case.

Also, for info: after the nested stop the outer run keeps executing guest code with c->stop already UNDEF; nothing in the loop tests c->stop, so a recovered stop is invisible until another failure. If that is intended, a comment in n2a32_run would help.
